extracted.intended_audience: educators, teachers, curriculum planners, and students of education
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and evaluative criteria for selecting subject matter and methods in school curricula that foster democratic, social, and intellectual development. Focuses on how to organize content, motivate learners, and cultivate intellectual habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Straightforwardness (trait of good method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method, expressed as an attitude of the individual, should feature straightforwardness as a trait of good method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method ought to follow the natural course of experience rather than being formal or artificial. Straightforwardness implies clear, direct organization of a learning sequence so learners can follow the development of meaning without unnecessary detours or concealed motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible intellectual interest / open-minded will to learn
rubrics_metrics.description: Good method requires 'flexible intellectual interest or open-minded will to learn.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage curiosity and adaptability; instruction should allow learners to follow emergent interests and adjust inquiry paths rather than rigidly enforcing preset sequences. Avoid curricular designs that stifle or ignore students' spontaneous intellectual engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrity of purpose is a central trait of good method: details should be subordinated to a unity of purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design lessons so every detail serves a clear educational end. Resist collecting disconnected facts or exercises that do not advance a coherent objective; value 'seeing a thing through' rather than mechanical completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of responsibility for consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Good intellectual attitude includes 'acceptance of responsibility for the consequences of one's activity including thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate dispositions where learners consider probable consequences of their beliefs and actions and deliberately account for them. Teach students to follow up ideas into conduct, not merely assent verbally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method must be rooted in real experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Method should be 'derived ... from observation of the course of experiences where there is no conscious distinction of personal attitude and manner from material dealt with.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating method as separate, formal machinery. Effective instruction grows from observed patterns of experience and integrates learners' attitudes with content. Anti-patterns: purely formal or mechanical instruction divorced from learners' lived situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating a split between private concealment and public avowal
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should not foster a split between 'avowed, public, and socially responsible undertakings, and private, ill-regulated, and suppressed indulgences of thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices like stern discipline, heavy reliance on extrinsic rewards, making schooling merely preparatory, or overemphasis on drill promote furtive, demoralizing attitudes and fragmented mental life. Aim to integrate learners' genuine interests with public, accountable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual responsibility (disposition to foresee and accept consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual responsibility is 'the disposition to consider in advance the probable consequences of any projected step and deliberately to accept them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build severe standards through practice in following up meaning into action. Guard against 'lazy acquiescence' where observation or assent is superficial. Assessment should reward evidence of considered acceptance and practical follow-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual thoroughness — seeing a thing through
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual thoroughness is 'seeing a thing through'—unity of purpose to which details are subordinated rather than mechanical drill on isolated steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate learning by the depth and firmness with which the full meaning of a purpose is developed. Discourage exhaustive drill whose only result is mechanical performance without integrated understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer fewer facts worked into deep situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Better to have 'fewer facts and truths in instruction' if a smaller number of situations can be intellectually worked out so conviction is real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize depth and the working out of situations that lead to conviction over breadth that produces superficial acquaintance. Overly congested curricula cause nervous strain and fail to develop genuine belief or identification with conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher must know subject matter and pupil capacities
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher should know subject matter thoroughly 'but be occupied ... in its interaction with the pupils' present needs and capacities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple scholarship is insufficient. Effective teachers understand both the mature, organized form of knowledge and the learner's present, practical organization (e.g., child's home as organizing center). Avoid projecting adult organization without adapting to learner's standpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational material must grow from student concerns and fit into acquaintance
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is educative only if 'it grow[s] naturally out of some question with which the student is concerned' and 'fit[s] into his more direct acquaintance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use information to deepen and connect to learners' existing experience; if not so connected it becomes 'mere words' and fosters rote memorization. Anti-pattern: swamping pupils with communicated material that overlays but does not integrate with personal experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach science as method and rational organization, not mere abstract facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Science is characterized by method and 'rationalized knowledge'—organizational relations that 'lead to and confirm' one another; the primacy of method defines scientific subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make scientific education emphasize inquiry, methods of testing, and logical interconnection rather than presenting abstract, remote facts. Otherwise scientific material becomes aloof and fails to teach the difference between opinion and warranted conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start curriculum with active occupations — learning by doing
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary subject matter exists as 'content of intelligent ability—power to do'; the initial stage of learning should be 'learning by doing' (arts and occupations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin instruction with practical, activity-based situations that connect to learners' impulses to explore and manipulate. This grounds later informational and scientific knowledge. Anti-pattern: treating early education as memorization of abstract facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter selection guided by social worth and essentials first
rubrics_metrics.description: The curriculum must 'take account of the adaptation of studies to the needs of the existing community life'—select with intention of improving communal life and 'place essentials first, and refinements second.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize broadly human, socially fundamental material over narrowly specialized or elitist traditions. Design curricula to develop capacities needed for participation in democratic social life rather than only vocational or class-based ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate play and constructive occupations into the curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Play, games, and constructive occupations similar to those children engage in outside school should be part of the regular program because they engage the whole pupil and connect school life with life out of school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use play and productive work not merely as diversion, but as vehicles for educative ends: increase motivation, reduce management burdens, provide social settings for cooperative learning, and afford motives for attention. Avoid treating them as token relief from 'regular' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overemphasis on drill and extrinsic rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: Exaggerated emphasis upon drill for automatic skill and motivation through 'rewards extraneous to the thing to be done' undermines genuine intellectual engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely primarily on mechanical drill, stern discipline, or extrinsic incentives; these produce vacuums in which native spontaneous mental traits become unused and lead to furtive, undisciplined thought. Prefer activities that enlist intrinsic motives and meaningful engagement.
